newsitem.title: USA: K.C. Southern sees growth via Mexican rail.
newsitem.headline: K.C. Southern sees growth via Mexican rail.

text.p: Kansas City Southern Industries Inc said it sees an opportunity to take more share of Mexico's freight transit via a concession to operate, along with a Mexican partner, one of the the nation's key railways.
The Northeast Railway links Laredo, Texas with Monterrey and Mexico City and the key ports of Veracruz, Tampico and Lazaro Cardenas, the company said.

On Friday, Kansas City Southern and joint venture partner Transportacion Maritima Mexicana SA de CV, or TMM, won a 50-year concession to operate the railway. It was the first privatization of a major Mexican rail line.
The Kansas City Southern-TMM joint venture -- Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana, or TFM -- bid $1.4 billion for the concession and bested two other bidders.

Shortly after the award was announced, Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp said they placed under review for possible downgrade the long-term debt ratings of TMM and Kansas City Southern.

At the same time, railroad analysts worried about how the joint venture could afford to pay the millions of dollars it will owe the Mexican government. Kansas City Southern shares were off one at 47 Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We see significant opportunity for increased rail traffic on the line," said a spokeswoman for Kansas City Southern, which posted 1995 revenues of $500 million and profits of $76.4 million, or $5.41 per share.
The company operates freight railways and mutual funds.
About 12 percent of Mexican freight moves by rail, as compared to 40 percent in the United States, the company said.
Through sister rail lines and its own routes, Kansas City Southern said it sees a chance to improve rail links between Mexico and the U.S. Midwest and Southeast.
